chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurarah and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), they both said:

We asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had relations with his wife during the month of Ramadan, and he had relations with her while he was in the state of Ihram (for Hajj or Umrah), and he did not think except that it was permissible for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no penalty upon him.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who has intercourse with his wife during Ramadan while in Ihram if he believes it is permissible?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the ruling of *jahil* (ignorance) in the context of Ramadan fasting, specifically addressing a man who engages in intercourse during the day while also in the state of Ihram. The Imam rules that there is no specific penalty (*kaffarah*) upon him, highlighting the principle that sincere belief in permissibility can exempt one from the standard expiation for breaking the fast. This case is often discussed alongside the more common scenario of intercourse during Ramadan to distinguish between the penalties for fasting violation versus Ihram violation when combined with ignorance.
